speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any short stature or specific dental abnormalities, such as missing teeth or enamel defects?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (Specifically 21-hydroxylase deficiency or 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency causing virilization and potential delayed puberty due to hormonal imbalance). The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (labial fusion, clitoromegaly), hirsutism in the mother, severe acne, and bone fragility suggests a genetic enzyme deficiency affecting cortisol and androgen synthesis. I will request specific hormonal panels to confirm the specific enzyme defect. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, 11-deoxycortisol, and ACTH stimulation test.
